billing.annual_refund.question: How do annual subscription refunds work?
billing.annual_refund.answer: When cancelling an annual subscription, used months are recalculated at the same plan’s monthly rate, and the positive balance of the annual amount actually paid is refunded. Example: subscribed for 12 months and used 3 → refund = annual amount paid minus 3 monthly payments, not 9/12 of the total. If no positive balance remains, no refund is due under this calculation. support.pro.faq.planned_dose_edit.q: Can I edit a planned dose without deleting the performed session?
support.pro.faq.planned_dose_edit.a: Yes. In the weekly microcycle, use the session pencil to edit duration and target sRPE. Saving refreshes the microcycle and planned versus perceived comparison while preserving perceived load and performed-session data. The session date and track stay unchanged.
support.pro.faq.daily_readiness.q: Is readiness reported for every activity?
support.pro.faq.daily_readiness.a: No. Each patient has one readiness/PSR response per day. Reopening the check-in locks saved scores; Adjust today's answers edits the same response. Each session has its own perceived load. Without a planned duration, the microcycle displays perceived load without inventing a target or adherence verdict. Answered sessions are marked as recorded in the check-in.
support.pro.faq.rf24.q: How do I compare perceived recovery (PSR) and recorded load?
support.pro.faq.rf24.a: Under Load and readiness, daily load bars (duration × RPE summed across tracks) are paired with a line for perceived recovery (PSR), the first check-in item scored 1–10. PSR is distinct from composite readiness. The seven displayed days are contextualized with acute load, the preceding seven-day period and the 28-day weekly average when enough history exists. Descriptive readings highlight PSR at least 2 points below/above the mean of at least 3 prior responses in seven days alongside acute load ±10% versus the previous seven-day period or ACWR outside 0.8–1.3. These are descriptive criteria, not diagnostic thresholds or statistical correlation. PSR may precede training; missing records do not mean rest. Consider symptoms, sleep and planning. There are no automatic adjustments or AI credits. Older responses used the training-readiness wording and are not retrospective PSR measurements.

ftest.title: Functional Tests
ftest.subtitle: Perform each test following the instructions and report if there was pain or discomfort.
ftest.question: How was the test?
ftest.no_tests_desc: No specific tests found for the selected regions.
ftest.cervical_rotation.name: Cervical Rotation
ftest.cervical_rotation.instruction: Seated with good posture, slowly rotate your head to the right and then to the left, trying to bring your chin toward your shoulder. Note any pain, limitation, or difference between sides.
ftest.cervical_flexion.name: Cervical Flexion & Extension
ftest.cervical_flexion.instruction: Seated, bring your chin toward your chest (flexion) then look up at the ceiling (extension). Perform slowly and note any pain or limitation.
ftest.upper_trap_stretch.name: Upper Trapezius Stretch
ftest.upper_trap_stretch.instruction: Seated, tilt your head to the right bringing your ear toward your shoulder. Hold 15 seconds. Repeat on the other side. Note excessive tension or pain.
ftest.deep_neck_flexor.name: Deep Neck Flexor Test
ftest.deep_neck_flexor.instruction: Lying face up, perform a gentle chin tuck and try to lift your head 2cm off the surface. Hold 10 seconds. Note tremor or difficulty.
ftest.cervical_trigger_points.name: Cervical Trigger Points
ftest.cervical_trigger_points.instructio: Using a tennis ball against the wall, press the lateral neck and base of skull area. Hold pressure for 20 seconds on tender points. Note if pain radiates elsewhere.
ftest.shoulder_flexion.name: Shoulder Flexion
ftest.shoulder_flexion.instruction: Standing, raise your arm in front of your body overhead. Keep the arm straight. Note at which angle pain or limitation appears.
ftest.shoulder_rotation.name: Shoulder Rotation
ftest.shoulder_rotation.instruction: With elbow at 90° and tucked to your side, rotate your forearm outward (external rotation) then bring your hand behind your back (internal rotation). Compare both sides.
ftest.pec_stretch.name: Pectoral Stretch
ftest.pec_stretch.instruction: Standing next to a doorway, place your forearm on the frame with elbow at shoulder height. Rotate your body away. Hold 20 seconds. Note tension or pain in chest/shoulder.
ftest.shoulder_isometric.name: Shoulder Isometric Test
ftest.shoulder_isometric.instruction: With elbow at 90° tucked to side, push your hand against a wall outward (external rotation). Hold 10 seconds. Repeat pushing inward. Note pain or weakness.
ftest.scapular_stability.name: Scapular Stability
ftest.scapular_stability.instruction: Perform a wall push-up. Observe if your shoulder blades wing out or protrude from your back. Note asymmetry between sides.
ftest.thoracic_rotation.name: Thoracic Rotation
ftest.thoracic_rotation.instruction: Seated with arms crossed on chest, rotate your trunk right then left. Keep hips still. Note limitation or pain.
ftest.thoracic_extension.name: Thoracic Extension
ftest.thoracic_extension.instruction: Seated with hands behind head, arch your back over the chair backrest. Move slowly. Note stiffness or pain in the mid-back region.
ftest.lumbar_flexion.name: Lumbar Flexion
ftest.lumbar_flexion.instruction: Standing, bend forward trying to touch your toes without bending your knees. Note where pain appears and how far you can reach.
ftest.lumbar_extension.name: Lumbar Extension
ftest.lumbar_extension.instruction: Standing with hands on hips, arch your back backward. Move slowly. Note if it worsens or relieves your lower back pain.
ftest.hamstring_flexibility.name: Hamstring Flexibility
ftest.hamstring_flexibility.instruction: Lying face up, raise one straight leg toward the ceiling. Keep the other leg on the floor. Note the angle reached and any pain behind the thigh.
ftest.core_endurance.name: Core Endurance
ftest.core_endurance.instruction: Lying face up with knees bent, lift your head and shoulders off the floor while pressing your lower back down. Hold 30 seconds. Note tremor or inability to maintain.
ftest.single_leg_balance.name: Single Leg Balance
ftest.single_leg_balance.instruction: Standing, lift one foot off the ground and maintain balance for 30 seconds. Repeat on the other side. Note instability or pain.
ftest.slump_test.name: Slump Test
ftest.slump_test.instruction: Seated on edge of chair, slouch forward and bring chin to chest. Then straighten one knee. Note if pain radiates down the leg (may indicate neural tension).
ftest.mckenzie_extension.name: McKenzie Extension
ftest.mckenzie_extension.instruction: Lying face down, prop up on elbows then hands, arching your back. Hold 5 seconds and repeat 10 times. Note if pain centralizes (improves) or peripheralizes (worsens).
ftest.lumbar_trigger_points.name: Lumbar Trigger Points
ftest.lumbar_trigger_points.instruction: Lying down, place a tennis ball under your lower back and glutes. Roll slowly seeking tender points. Hold pressure 20-30 seconds per point. Note referred pain.
ftest.hip_flexion.name: Hip Flexion
ftest.hip_flexion.instruction: Lying face up, pull one knee toward your chest with hands. Note limitation or pain in the groin/hip. Compare both sides.
ftest.hip_rotation.name: Hip Rotation
ftest.hip_rotation.instruction: Lying with knees bent at 90°, let leg fall inward (internal rotation) and outward (external rotation). Note pain or limitation in each direction.
ftest.hip_flexor_stretch.name: Hip Flexor Stretch
ftest.hip_flexor_stretch.instruction: Kneel with one knee on the ground and other foot forward. Push hips forward keeping trunk upright. Hold 20 seconds. Note tension in front of thigh/hip.
ftest.glute_bridge.name: Glute Bridge
ftest.glute_bridge.instruction: Lying face up with knees bent, lift hips off floor squeezing glutes. Hold 10 seconds. Note weakness, asymmetry, or pain.
ftest.knee_flexion_extension.name: Knee Flexion & Extension
ftest.knee_flexion_extension.instruction: Seated, fully extend your knee then bend it as far as possible. Note crepitus (clicking), pain, or limitation of motion.
ftest.quad_flexibility.name: Quadriceps Flexibility
ftest.quad_flexibility.instruction: Standing, hold your ankle and pull heel toward glute. Hold 20 seconds. Note excessive tension or pain in front of thigh.
ftest.single_leg_squat.name: Single Leg Squat
ftest.single_leg_squat.instruction: Standing on one leg, squat slowly to 45°. Note if knee caves inward, if there's pain or instability. Compare both sides.
ftest.knee_stability.name: Knee Stability
ftest.knee_stability.instruction: Standing on one leg, perform small knee bends (mini squats). Note if knee wobbles side to side or if there's a feeling of giving way.
ftest.single_leg_balance_ankle.name: Single Leg Balance (30 seconds)
ftest.single_leg_balance_ankle.instructi: Standing, lift one foot off the ground and maintain balance for 30 seconds. Repeat on the other side. Compare stability between sides. Note instability, swaying, or inability to complete the 30 seconds.
ftest.weight_bearing_lunge_test.name: Weight-Bearing Lunge Test
ftest.weight_bearing_lunge_test.instruct: Standing facing a wall with the test foot forward. Lunge your knee toward the wall without lifting the heel. Progressively move the foot back until you find the maximum distance where the knee still touches the wall. Measure the distance from big toe to wall. Compare both sides — differences greater than 1.5cm may be significant.
ftest.heel_rise_test.name: Heel Rise Test
ftest.heel_rise_test.instruction: Standing on one leg with hand lightly resting on a wall for balance, rise onto tiptoe as high as possible and lower slowly. Repeat until fatigue or up to 25 reps. Count repetitions on each side and compare. Fewer than 20 reps may indicate triceps surae weakness.
ftest.questionnaire_overlap_notice: Some movements already addressed in the questionnaire may be requested again in this step. This is normal — functional tests evaluate different aspects of the same ability.
ftest.wrist_flexion_extension.name: Wrist Flexion & Extension
ftest.wrist_flexion_extension.instructio: With forearm supported, bend your wrist up and down fully. Note pain, limitation, or difference between hands.
ftest.grip_strength.name: Grip Strength
ftest.grip_strength.instruction: Squeeze a rolled towel with maximum force for 10 seconds. Note pain in wrist, elbow, or forearm. Compare both hands.
ftest.neural_tension_upper.name: Upper Limb Neural Tension
ftest.neural_tension_upper.instruction: Standing, extend arm to the side at shoulder height palm up. Extend wrist (fingers pointing down) and tilt head to the opposite side. Note tingling or pain radiating down the arm.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.faq1.q: What is this self-assessment and how does it work?
faq.faq1.a: It is an online musculoskeletal self-assessment: you fill in the answers yourself, guided by a clinical method designed by a specialist physiotherapist. The system presents questions about your pain, functional tests and generates a preliminary clinical hypothesis with a personalized treatment plan. It is not a clinical consultation — it is a screening and health-education tool.
faq.faq2.q: Why should I invest in the premium self-assessment?
faq.faq2.a: The premium version includes a complete anamnesis, video-guided functional tests, scientifically validated questionnaires, a detailed hypothesis with explanation, a 3-phase treatment plan and a PDF report — all generated from your own answers, processed by the app’s clinical method.
faq.faq3.q: Who is the physiotherapist behind the method?
faq.faq3.a: The clinical reasoning method that guides the self-assessment was designed by a physiotherapist specialized in Orthopedic and Sports Physiotherapy, with a postgraduate degree and over 7 years of clinical experience. Important: the professional does not treat you directly — he designed the protocol that the system applies automatically.
faq.faq4.q: Does this self-assessment replace an in-person consultation?
faq.faq4.a: No. The self-assessment is a screening and educational guidance tool. It helps you understand your pain and direct your treatment, but it does not replace in-person medical or physiotherapy diagnosis, nor does it establish a professional-patient clinical relationship. In serious cases, always seek in-person care.
faq.faq5.a: Yes! With the premium version, you can redo the self-assessment once within 7 days of purchase, allowing you to track your progress and adjust treatment as needed.
faq.faq6.q: What if the screening detects red flags?
faq.faq6.a: Your safety comes first. In the premium self-assessment, the red flag screening happens BEFORE payment. If you answer YES to any critical question, the flow is interrupted immediately, you are guided to seek in-person medical evaluation, and you are NOT charged. The screening questions and answers are stored on your profile and shown in the PDF as proof. For monthly subscribers, this case does not consume a self-assessment from your plan.
faq.faq7.q: Why can't I select all the body regions I want?
faq.faq7.a: The system uses clinical reasoning based on kinetic chains — structures that are biomechanically connected. Regions from the same body segment (e.g., shoulder and elbow) can be assessed together because they influence each other. Regions from different segments (e.g., foot and neck) require separate assessments to ensure accuracy of the preliminary clinical hypothesis and a precise treatment plan.

support.patient.tool.basic_assessment.de: The basic assessment is free and allows you to complete a guided questionnaire about your pain. The premium assessment includes detailed anamnesis, red flag screening, validated questionnaires, pain map, functional tests, and an AI-generated preliminary clinical hypothesis with a personalized treatment plan. The safety screening is an integral part of the assessment — if red flags are identified, the assessment is considered completed and in-person medical referral is essential. Requires an active monthly subscription or single payment.

support.patient.faq.pf1.q: Can I do more than one self-assessment?

support.patient.faq.pf2.a: Yes. All data is stored with encryption and restricted to your account. No data is shared with third parties without your consent.

support.patient.faq.pf4.q: How does the treatment plan work?

support.patient.faq.pf5.q: Can I cancel my subscription at any time?

Access remains active until the end of the paid period. For annual plans, on cancellation, used months are deducted at the plan’s monthly rate; the positive balance of the annual amount paid is refunded.
support.patient.faq.pf6.q: What happens if I have red flags in the premium self-assessment?
support.patient.faq.pf6.a: Under the new flow, the red flag screening happens BEFORE the premium self-assessment payment. If you answer YES to any critical question (severe trauma, unexplained weight loss, relentless night pain, progressive numbness, recent surgery in the painful region with plates/screws/prosthesis, etc.), the flow is interrupted immediately, you are guided to seek in-person medical evaluation, and you are NOT charged — no amount is debited, and for monthly subscribers this case does not consume a self-assessment from your plan. Before being blocked, you can still review your answers (in case you marked YES out of doubt). All screening questions and answers are stored in the database and shown in the PDF as proof. Your safety is always the priority.
support.patient.faq.pf7.a: Yes. You can start a new self-assessment at any time within your plan limits. Previous self-assessment history remains saved for comparison.
support.patient.faq.pf8.a: No, it's optional. However, keeping a daily pain log helps identify patterns and track progress, making future self-assessments more accurate.

support.pro.tool.edit_profile.desc: Keep your data updated: name, CREFITO, specialties, city, clinic address, and profile photo. This information is displayed to patients in the professional search.
support.pro.tool.lifetime_treatment.desc: With Lifetime Treatment, all your patients' treatment plans are permanently unlocked — no additional cost per assessment, from the purchase date onward. Important: access to the professional panel still requires an active PRO subscription (monthly or annual). Lifetime Treatment does not replace the panel subscription.
support.pro.tool.acquire_treatment_badge: Treatment Plan sale removed from the dashboard

The 'Unlock Treatment' badge and one-off purchase cards are no longer shown in PRO and clinic dashboards. Prescribe the home exercise program (HEP) via the Clinical Reasoning Agent or the Exercises module in the patient record.
support.pro.tool.messages.title: Messages with Patients
support.pro.tool.messages.desc: Patients who found you through the professional search or who requested a referral can send direct messages. Conversations appear in the 'Messages' tab of your panel. ⚠️ Important: Aliv.iA is not responsible for personal data shared, appointments, financial agreements, or any arrangements made via messages on the platform. The messaging feature is provided as an auxiliary communication tool.
support.pro.tool.clinical_impression.des: The clinical impression generated or written in the manual assessment appears in the patient record as soon as the assessment is saved, including objectives and professional edits, without a second generation or credit consumption. It is also included in the professional PDF. New data does not automatically replace the saved impression: use 'Regenerate' when you want to update the analysis. If no impression exists, use 'Generate Clinical Impression'.
support.pro.tool.hep.title: Exercise Program (HEP)
support.pro.tool.hep.desc: In the patient evolution panel, click 'Create Exercise Program'. Select from 70+ exercises (home and gym), set sets, reps and frequency, or add custom exercises manually. A public link is generated for the patient to access on their phone with instructional videos, no login needed. Valid for 90 days. When creating or editing a HEP, the summary estimates intensity and effective weekly sets per region: strength ×1, stabilization/proprioception ×0.5; mobility/flexibility are excluded from this count. Choose physiotherapy, gym or other sport. Saving updates the planned dose in future sessions of the linked microcycle, preserving past sessions. Target effort between 5 and 9 is an estimate; actual effort is reported by the patient. The physiotherapist retains the decision.
support.pro.tool.hep_templates.title: Reusable HEP templates
support.pro.tool.hep_templates.desc: Save exercise programs as custom templates and reuse them for new patients. Includes pre-built templates (e.g., shoulder progression) and your own templates that you create and edit. After applying a template, you can remove individual exercises if they are contraindicated for that patient.
support.pro.tool.studio_carousel.title: Studio: carousels and post threads
support.pro.tool.studio_offer_ribbon.des: In Create, select Oferta / faixas diagonais: crossed ribbons, a large headline and a highlighted offer in your brand colors. Uses offers declared in the kit, without copying discounts or dates from the reference. Supports text editing, saving and PNG download.
support.pro.tool.studio_carousel.desc: Studio can also present a carousel as a sequence of short brand posts with a beginning, development, and conclusion. Each slide keeps its own download, save, text editing, and color inversion controls.
support.pro.tool.studio_creative_network: Before writing, Studio connects audience, scene, problem, explanation, proof, and next step. In Aliv.iA Differentials, each artwork stays within one feature and automatically reuses validated messaging from the brand pages — such as continuity without rework, safety, concrete deliverables, and connection with a physiotherapist — without adding new controls. Incomplete titles, cut-off conclusions, loose technical lists, and repeated highlights are rejected. For veterinary brands, the copy addresses the owner while keeping the pet at the center of the complaint, investigation, and progress. Any brand can create its own editorial line with topics that can be selected together. Generation is local and consumes no extra AI credits. Lists and comparisons remove repeated or very similar arguments, keeping complementary ideas within the same topic without inventing filler items. In Create, copied, downloaded and saved captions follow the artwork’s own text, including manual edits, without standalone objections or unrelated arguments. Natural writing preserves complete sentences; numbers, ranges and clinical facts bypass rhetorical rewriting. Benefits linked to the core offer and each audience’s desires take priority over ancillary functions. The hook library uses arguments from all registered audiences, preserving their calls to action and evidence, without promising outcomes or spending AI credits per artwork. For software, including Aliv.iA, 90% of batch publications prioritize what the product is and does, its differentiators and practical use linked to benefits. Carousels count as one publication; small batches round up. Only declared, audience-scoped capabilities are used, without inventing functions or autonomous AI; sparse kits receive no fictional content. Background photos have a 0–100% shading control, including no film, per batch and artwork; the setting follows PNG exports and gallery edits. Hospitality uses declared house and stay facts, without software language or outcome promises. Active hooks for the selected topic rotate with priority for unused entries; hospitality no longer replaces the library with a few house facts. Disabled hooks remain excluded from generation.
support.pro.tool.studio_cardiorespirator: For the Aliv.iA brand, select the Cardiovascular monitoring, Cardiorespiratory assessment or Cardiorespiratory report differentials. In the Solution ecosystem model, choose “Monitorizar, avaliar e explicar o esforço”. The journey connects data from a wristband, watch, chest strap or pulse oximeter to supervised tests and reports with explicit protocols and references. Screenshot readings require review: there is no automatic device connection or autonomous diagnosis. Tests accept screenshots directly and do not duplicate weekly load. Artwork generation is local, without extra AI credits.
support.pro.tool.studio_ecosystem.title: Studio: Solution ecosystem
support.pro.tool.studio_ecosystem.desc: For the Aliv.iA brand, choose the Solution ecosystem model to connect three to five features into one journey. Use one of ten suggested chains (professional, clinic and patient) or adjust its steps and order. Each generation delivers six visual arguments and one complete carousel with the same audience, promise, and conclusion, without extra AI credits. Includes monitoring → functional assessment → cardiorespiratory report.
support.pro.tool.ai_test_suggestions.des: During the manual assessment, the AI analyzes the anamnesis, pain regions, and questionnaires filled in previous steps and suggests 2 to 6 additional clinical tests (orthopedic, mobility, neurodynamic, or functional). Clicking a suggestion automatically inserts the test into the functional tests field as inspiration for the professional.
support.pro.tool.reassessment.title: Reassessment and comparison
support.pro.tool.reassessment.desc: Start a new assessment for the same patient to document follow-up. With two or more completed assessments, the panel compares pain, functional questionnaires, ROM and dynamometry over time and enables an evolution report.
support.pro.tool.white_label.title: Brand on Reports (White-label)
support.pro.tool.white_label.desc: In your professional profile, upload your logo. It will automatically appear on exported PDFs (header and footer) and on the assessment screen when the patient fills it via your personalized link. Reinforce your professional identity in every delivery. In clinic mode, the institutional name, logo and color take priority in assessment/evolution, cardiovascular and microcycle reports, and check-in, reassessment, questionnaire and HEP links; the responsible professional remains identified.
support.pro.tool.evolution_report.title: Evolution / Discharge Report
support.pro.tool.evolution_report.desc: In the patient evolution panel, when there are 2 or more completed assessments, click 'Evolution Report'. Before generating, you choose the scope of the comparison: a quick period filter (last 30/60/90 days, counted from the most recent assessment) or manually picking which assessments to include — so older clinical pictures don't get mixed into the current one. The system compares the first and last assessment within the selected range: pain scores (VAS), functional questionnaires, dynamometry/ROM and session notes from the period. AI generates a clinical narrative summary with percentage variations and a recommendation (Discharge, Continue or Reassess). The PDF is exported with your brand and can be shared via WhatsApp — ideal for justifying discharge, renewing insurance authorizations or demonstrating results to patients.
support.pro.tool.simulated_env.title: Simulated Environment (Demo Mode)
support.pro.tool.clinic_demo.title: Clinic demo: load and organization
support.pro.tool.clinic_demo.updated_sce: The PRO and clinic demos show all six STEPS stages, planned activities and recovery days, filtered local history and dose/readiness variations. Discharged patients remain in maintenance; patients without a history receive no invented data. The Agent offers in-depth scripted discussions and Insights are categorized, using fictional patient signals and schedule values without AI usage or real patient writes.
support.pro.tool.clinic_demo.clinical_al: Load scenarios follow each fictional patient's latest assessment, including phase, pain, restrictions and health alerts. Doses and readiness are illustrative, not prescriptions or real measurements.
support.pro.tool.clinic_demo.desc: The public clinic demo includes fictional load history, an sRPE × PSR chart, ACWR, daily guidance, dose and microcycle in the patient record. Planning and recording sessions stays in the demo, without saving real data or spending AI credits. View as switches between owner, therapist (assigned patients and schedule), and secretary (reception, assignment and attendance confirmation, without clinical records). The team also includes an administrator, student/intern and osteopath. Switching views does not change your account or real permissions. The record's Summary button shows hypothesis, clinical impression, daily guidance, microcycle, load × PSR chart, latest progress note and latest exercise program.
support.pro.tool.simulated_env.desc: When you subscribe to the PRO plan, you get access to the Simulated Environment — a complete replica of the professional panel with 5 fictional patients and realistic clinical data. You can explore all features without affecting real data: view complete assessments with validated questionnaires (Oswestry, NDI, DASH, LEFS, SPADI), generate AI clinical impressions, review detailed treatment plans, compare assessments in the evolution dashboard, and generate evolution reports. Use the 'Pro Panel / Simulated Panel' toggle at the top of the panel to switch between real data and the demo environment. Ideal for getting familiar with the platform before receiving your first patients.
support.pro.tool.insights_churn.title: Silent dropout (churn risk)
support.pro.tool.insights_churn.desc: In the Insights tab, the system cross-references recent no-shows, missing upcoming appointments, stagnant pain in readiness check-ins and inactivity — days without a recorded session (completed slot or record note) and without check-ins. Full inactivity weighs more in the 0-100 score because it usually precedes dropout. Pain diary and internal messages are not used: in practice few patients use those channels. Each patient shows the reasons and days without activity, with shortcuts to reschedule or message. The list scrolls internally with per-patient dismissal and restoration; owner/admin can dismiss for the team.
support.pro.tool.insights_flareup.title: Flare-up & overload
support.pro.tool.insights_flareup.desc: Cross-references pain reported in readiness check-ins with training load: a flare-up is the latest check-in pain (within 3 days) at least 2 points above the 30-day average, with 3+ check-ins. The card also shows ACWR (acute ÷ chronic load, ideal 0.8-1.3) and readiness drops. A pain spike combined with ACWR above 1.3 raises the case to high risk.
support.pro.tool.insights_reassessment.d: Lists patients 28+ days without a completed assessment, or with 8+ session notes since the last one. Reassessing documents progress, refreshes the plan and supports the continuity or discharge conversation. Each item can be dismissed with the X and restored later — dismissal only applies to you.
support.pro.tool.insights_steps.title: Treatment phase (STEPS)
support.pro.tool.insights_steps.desc: Shows the current macrocycle phase of each active periodization plan and how many weeks the patient has been in it. Anyone over 4 weeks in the same phase is highlighted — a signal to review exit criteria and progress. Tap a patient to change the phase or record Discharge (which closes the plan) without opening the record. Discharge also appears as the phase in the record summary, preserving previous phases in history. Each item can be dismissed with the X and restored later — dismissal only applies to you.
support.pro.tool.insights_management.tit: Insights by category and management metrics
support.pro.tool.insights_management.des: The Insights tab is organized in sub-tabs (Overview, Patients, Clinical routine, Finance, Team & Quality, Operations). A realized session counts from a completed slot OR a same-day record note — metrics don't go empty when the team skips agenda classification. Records up to date: note within 48h; past slots never classified (done/no-show/cancelled) and without a note count as pending, never as 'on time'. Finance uses the clinic's service catalog (Insights > Operations > Services & pricing): per-service prices, per-session or monthly (monthly fee diluted per realized session that month), with the service picked when booking; without a service, the default price applies. Metrics: clinical LTV, empty-chair cost, revenue per clinical hour, discharge vs dropout per therapist, real vs prescribed frequency, organic referral, no next appointment, late cancellation (<2h, measured from the status-change timestamp; slots without a time stay 'no recorded time' and the window follows the cancellation date), owner dependence and capacity bottleneck (rooms × therapists; solo PROs see schedule occupancy instead of saturation). Finance and Team only for owner/admin and solo PRO. Computed locally, no AI credits. Frequency compares completed and expected sessions only for elapsed days this month, since registration or first session, whichever is later. LTV expands patient sessions with date, time and value; empty-chair cost details each absence/cancellation. Missing times are identified, never invented. Grey personal commitments remain in the Calendar but never enter Insights metrics: occupancy, no-shows, revenue, goals, team or care-session counts. Notes linked to these commitments do not count as care sessions either.
support.pro.tool.insights_funnel.title: Assessment → appointment conversion
support.pro.tool.insights_funnel.desc: In clinic and solo PRO, shows patients whose first completed assessment in the profile was within 90 days: with a treatment appointment within 7 days of the assessment, without a confirmed appointment, and already attended — including the named list of who lacks an appointment within 7 days. Reassessments do not increase the base. Cancellations, no-shows, commitments and assessment appointments do not count as conversion. Matching uses email or linked assessment, not name alone; without an identifiable link conversion is not confirmed. List items can be dismissed with the X and restored later. Separate profile data, no AI credits.
support.pro.tool.insights_reactivation.d: Past patients with 2+ recorded visits (completed slot or record note), the last one 30-180 days ago, and no return booked. Unlike silent dropout (active patients cooling off), these are already-inactive contacts worth a win-back approach — with shortcuts to book or message.
support.pro.tool.insights_discharge.desc: Estimate of remaining sessions until discharge combining four signals when available: pain evolution from readiness check-ins (weight 40), current STEPS plan phase (30), workload progress over the last 4 weeks vs the previous 4 (15) and current readiness (15). Each patient shows path progress and the factors used; confidence grows with more signals and sessions. Helps plan packages, organize the schedule and prepare the discharge conversation.
support.pro.tool.insights_revenue.title: Revenue goal + 'what-if' simulator
support.pro.tool.insights_revenue.desc: Set your monthly revenue goal and average session price in Edit profile. The simulator shows how much you would earn if you reduced no-shows or increased occupancy by X percentage points — turning KPIs into practical decisions.
support.pro.tool.insights_adherence.desc: Combines completed HEP exercises, readiness check-in consistency and schedule attendance into a single 0-100 score per patient. Pain diary and message reads are not used: most patients don't use those channels day to day. The 'i' popup explains each variable's weight and lets you adjust them. Includes check-ins by patient ID even without email, with all patients searchable. Consistency uses 14 days to date; check-ins within 60 days keep the patient listed. Missing channels do not reduce the score.
support.pro.tool.insights_benchmark.desc: Compares your real KPIs (no-show, occupancy, assessments/month, average time to discharge, NPS) with the average of smaller, same-size and larger clinics. Other clinics' data is always anonymous and aggregated. Know if you're above or below the market and where to focus to grow — a unique differential of Aliv.iA Clinic.
support.pro.tool.ai_credits.title: AI credits control ('Your AI usage' widget)
support.pro.tool.ai_credits.desc: Included credits per month: PRO 30 on monthly and 33 on annual plans; Academic 20 on monthly and 22 on annual plans (10% annual bonus). Clinic: Small 80, Medium 150 and Large 250 total, shared by the team, never multiplied by staff. Included credits renew monthly on the Brasília calendar. Partners: 25 free credits/month and paid packs available. Only admin and VIP have unlimited use. Warnings at 80% and 100% appear during use and in Insights. Packs: 15/R$39, 30/R$69, 60/R$129, valid 12 months; used once monthly credits run out, never automatically charging a card. Only clinic owner/admin buys; the team shares the balance. Blocking remains disabled; when activated by category in Admin, insufficient balance opens renewal/purchase options without locking records.
support.pro.tool.voice_notes.title: Voice notes during manual assessment (AI)
support.pro.tool.voice_notes.desc: During a manual assessment in the clinic, a floating mic button lets you record your narrative while examining the patient — no need to stop and type. The audio is processed by AI (Gemini), automatically transcribed and summarized into structured clinical text saved on the patient's assessment. The raw audio is discarded for privacy — only the text remains. Reclaim real consultation time, capture clinical findings while you speak and build a rich chart even on the busiest days.
support.pro.tool.session_dictation.title: Dictate the patient's progress note
support.pro.tool.session_dictation.desc: In the chart, the progress-note field has a recording bar attached: tap "Dictate" and speak your treatment notes — the text appears in the field at every pause, exactly as spoken. Choose whether dictation goes to the progress note or the observation field, and pause, resume or discard at will. The same bar appears when editing any entry inside "Progress history". Audio is never stored: each segment is converted to text and discarded, and nothing is saved until you press save.
support.pro.tool.academic_mode.title: Academic Mode — Mentor, Quizzes, Cases, Tracks & XP
support.pro.tool.academic_mode.desc: In the Clinical Agent, students with active PRO, admin-enabled academic partners and PRO professionals get special commands: /professor turns on the Mentor persona (Socratic preceptor that reviews concepts before management); /quiz [topic] [n] generates an interactive quiz with explained answer key; /caso [topic] creates a complete fictitious patient in the 'Study cases' tab for practice; /traduzir [link or text] translates papers to pt-BR with PICO + evidence level; /trilha [topic] [1-5] delivers a didactic lesson for the selected Knowledge Track module (Shoulder, Lumbar, Hip, Knee, Cervical), without treating it as patient intake. Every correct quiz answer, completed module, resolved case or translated paper earns XP, which stacks per niche unlocking Apprentice → Practitioner → Specialist → Master badges. Track XP, badges and strong/weak topics in the 'Academic performance' card on My Account.
support.pro.tool.data_import.title: Import external data
support.pro.tool.data_import.desc: In My Account or clinic Management, import CSV/TSV, tabular TXT, JSON, XML or Aliv.iA ZIP. Combined categories separates patients, assessments and session notes using column blocks or a row-category column, with editable mapping. Review counts, dates, links and all issues; unknown columns require an explicit decision. Session notes still require a genuine patient email; external codes do not replace that link. Up to 20MB per file, 50 tables, 50,000 rows per table and 100 smaller batches per operation, also bounded by content size. Patients are imported before history. Conflicting identities block affected records. Partial import requires confirmation; a failed batch stops subsequent batches. Identical retries recover completed batches without duplication. Undo within 24h restores merges and removes created records; later changes block the entire operation. ZIP does not restore attachments, treatments, messages or permissions. Universal compatibility and FisioSoft-specific integration are not validated.
support.pro.tool.data_export.title: Export all data (.zip) — backup & data portability
support.pro.tool.data_export.desc: In My Account → "Privacy & data" section, the "Data backup, export & import" block generates a complete .zip with patients, assessments, appointments, professional notes, voice notes and an index of documents/photos (secure 1-hour signed links). You choose exactly which categories to include to keep the file small. Guarantees full data portability (LGPD/GDPR), an independent secondary backup and peace of mind: your records are YOURS, always exportable. Available for autonomous PRO professionals and clinic owners.
support.pro.tool.session_notes_quick.tit: Quick evolution logging in the record
support.pro.tool.session_notes_quick.des: Inside the patient record, the "Log evolution" button (header on desktop; floating button on mobile) scrolls to "Session notes" and opens the new-note form with the cursor ready in the text field. The "Session notes" shortcut in the record's side menu does the same.
support.pro.tool.final_hypothesis.title: Preliminary clinical hypothesis (override AI)
support.pro.tool.final_hypothesis.desc: You are the clinical decision-maker — you can agree with the AI's hypothesis or override it with your own preliminary clinical hypothesis. In the patient chart and assessment view, an editor lets you mark 'Agree with AI' or type a custom final hypothesis (up to 200 characters). When overridden, the final hypothesis is highlighted in the chart, fully replaces the AI suggestion in the patient PDF and WhatsApp share. The original AI suggestion stays visible internally as a discreet line below. Available for autonomous PRO professionals and for owners/therapists in Clinic mode (secretaries cannot edit).
support.pro.tool.rename_share_assessment: Each assessment can be renamed with a custom title (e.g., 'Initial assessment', '3-month reassessment'), making chart organization easier. The generated PDF inherits the chosen name — useful for email and physical record archiving. You can also share the assessment via WhatsApp (summary text with hypothesis and plan) or send the full PDF directly through the share button.
support.pro.tool.video_call.title: Video call with patients (P2P)
support.pro.tool.video_call.desc: Start video calls directly from chat with your active patients — P2P connection (WebRTC) via Supabase Realtime, no intermediate media server. The patient receives a push notification even when the app is closed and accepts through a pre-call screen (test camera/microphone first). System messages in chat log when the call starts and ends. Ideal for quick questions, demonstrating exercises, or follow-ups without formal scheduling. Available for active PRO professionals.
support.pro.faq.rf1.q: Does my patient need to create an Aliv.iA account?
support.pro.faq.rf1.a: Not necessarily. Using your personalized link, the patient can complete the assessment and the result is linked to your panel. However, if they want to access their history later, they'll need to create an account.
support.pro.faq.rf2.q: How do I cancel my PRO subscription?
support.pro.faq.rf2.a: Access your professional panel, click 'Manage subscription' and you'll be directed to the secure payment portal where you can cancel at any time. Access remains active until the end of the paid period. For annual plans, on cancellation, used months are deducted at the plan’s monthly rate; the positive balance of the annual amount paid is refunded.
support.pro.faq.rf3.a: Yes. The platform uses encryption and restricted access policies. Only you have access to assessments linked to your profile. Data follows security and privacy best practices.
support.pro.faq.rf4.q: Can I use Aliv.iA as a pre-consultation screening tool?
support.pro.faq.rf4.a: Yes, that's one of the main use cases. Send the link to the patient before the appointment so they complete the assessment. During the consultation, you'll already have anamnesis, questionnaires, and pain map filled in.
support.pro.faq.rf5.q: How many patients can I manage with the PRO plan?
support.pro.faq.rf5.a: There is no patient limit. All patients who complete an assessment via your link will appear in your panel automatically.
support.pro.faq.rf6.q: What does the patient evolution chart show?
support.pro.faq.rf6.a: The chart shows the top 3 functional limitation subscales and total questionnaire score, comparing all assessments over time. This makes it easy to visually demonstrate clinical progress.
support.pro.faq.rf7.q: Can I export all patient data?
support.pro.faq.rf7.a: Yes. Use the 'Export PDFs' button to generate batch reports of all assessments with a recorded preliminary clinical hypothesis. Each assessment generates an individual PDF.
support.pro.faq.rf8.q: Are the notes I add visible to the patient?
support.pro.faq.rf8.a: No. Professional notes are private and visible only to you in the panel. They are included in the exported PDF for clinical documentation purposes.
support.pro.faq.rf9.q: What is the Simulated Environment and how does it work?
support.pro.faq.rf9.a: The Simulated Environment is a demo mode available to all PRO subscribers. It features 5 fictional patients with complete, realistic clinical data — including validated questionnaires (Oswestry, NDI, DASH, LEFS, SPADI), preliminary clinical hypotheses, treatment plans, and AI clinical impressions. You can browse assessments, generate evolution reports, and test all features without affecting real data. To activate it, use the 'Pro Panel / Simulated Panel' toggle at the top of the professional panel. It's ideal for getting familiar with the platform before receiving your first patients.
support.pro.faq.rf10.q: Can I adjust the preliminary clinical hypothesis suggested by the AI?
support.pro.faq.rf10.a: Yes. In the patient chart or assessment view you'll see a 'Final Hypothesis (Professional)' card with two options: agree with the AI suggestion (keeps current behavior) or manually type your own hypothesis. The final hypothesis fully replaces the AI suggestion in the patient PDF, WhatsApp share, and any chart highlight — but the original AI suggestion stays visible to you, internally, below the revised hypothesis. You can edit it or revert to the AI suggestion at any time. In Clinic mode, only owners and therapists have permission; secretaries don't see the editor.
support.pro.faq.rf11.q: What if the internet drops in the middle of a manual or patient assessment?
support.pro.faq.rf11.a: Everything is saved automatically. The assessment has offline auto-save with 800ms debounce — every answer, pain map mark, and questionnaire is stored locally in the browser. If the connection drops, a discreet banner notifies you, but you continue assessing normally. When the internet returns, data syncs automatically. If the patient closes the browser mid-way (or you need to pause), just reopen from the same device: the system shows a summary of what's already filled and a 'Continue where I left off' button. No answer is lost.
support.pro.faq.rf12.q: Does the video call require a paid server, plugin, or separate app?
support.pro.faq.rf12.a: No. The call uses WebRTC peer-to-peer — the connection is direct between your browser and the patient's, with no media server in between. Signaling (initial handshake) happens via Supabase Realtime, already included in your subscription. Works in the browser (desktop and mobile) without installing anything. Push notifications alert the patient even with the app closed, and both sides go through a pre-call screen to test camera/microphone before joining.
support.pro.faq.rf13.q: How do I prescribe exercises for an older assessment?
support.pro.faq.rf13.a: Use the Clinical Reasoning Agent or the Exercises (HEP) module in the patient record.
support.pro.faq.rf14.q: How do I cancel, resume or switch my subscription to annual?
support.pro.faq.rf14.a: All self-service: go to My Account → "Subscription & billing" → "My subscription" card. There you can see your plan, price, status and next billing date, and you can cancel (access stays until the end of the period you already paid for, never cut immediately), undo a scheduled cancellation, switch from monthly to annual (with prorated credit) or open the Stripe portal to change your card and view receipts. No need to contact support. Every change is logged and the Aliv.iA team is notified instantly. For annual plans, on cancellation, used months are deducted at the plan’s monthly rate; the positive balance of the annual amount paid is refunded.
support.pro.faq.rf15.q: Where are patient comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes, heart disease) and continuous medication recorded?
support.pro.faq.rf15.a: They are mandatory anamnesis questions in every flow — manual assessment, basic and premium self-assessment, and assessments through your professional/clinic link. They appear in the patient record, in every PDF report, and are sent to the AI clinical reasoning, which adapts exercise dosage and flags precautions (Valsalva, high-intensity isometrics, medical clearance when heart disease is present).
support.pro.faq.rf16.q: How do I apply the FABQ (fear-avoidance / catastrophising) and when is it indicated?
support.pro.faq.rf16.a: The Brazilian FABQ is a complementary questionnaire in the Psychosocial (yellow flags) domain — it depends on the patient profile, not on a body region. It appears in the "Complementary questionnaires" panel of manual and link-based assessments. AI suggests it for persistent pain, nociplastic mechanisms, high pain intensity, fear of movement, recurrence or sick leave, and you can also apply it manually. In a new assessment, apply it again to compare the Physical Activity and Work subscales. Results appear in the chart and PDF and feed the clinical reasoning.
support.patient.faq.pf_signup.q: Do I need to confirm my email to access my account?
support.patient.faq.pf_signup.a: No. When you sign up, you go straight into the app — no need to wait for a confirmation email. This avoids delays from providers that often filter our messages. Still, keep a valid email on your account because it's used for password recovery, reports and reminders.
support.pro.faq.rf_signup.q: Do I need to confirm my email to access my professional account?
support.pro.faq.rf_signup.a: No. When you sign up from the professional, clinic or patient landing page, you go straight into the dashboard — no email confirmation step. This removes the delay that providers like Hotmail/Outlook used to cause. Your email is still important for password recovery, Stripe receipts (if you subscribe to PRO/Clinic/Lifetime Treatment) and notifications.
support.pro.faq.rf_subscribe_first.q: Can I subscribe to PRO before entering my CREFITO?
support.pro.faq.rf_subscribe_first.a: Yes. On the PRO page, pick monthly or annual and click subscribe: if signed in, you go straight to payment; otherwise you create a quick account and continue to payment with your plan saved. After paying (or cancelling), you return to the PRO dashboard. Until you enter your CREFITO or enable Academic mode, the reasoning agent, agenda and patient creation are available; new assessments (manual or link) and exercise prescription are locked, with "Enter CREFITO" and "I'm a student" buttons. Your profile also stays out of the directory. Once completed, everything unlocks instantly with the same subscription.
support.pro.faq.rf_student.q: I'm a physiotherapy student without a CREFITO yet. Can I use Aliv.iA?
support.pro.faq.rf_student.a: Yes. In 'My Account' > 'Student Access — Aliv.iA Academic', turn on student mode and provide your full name, institution and term. This enables the academic seal, removes the CREFITO requirement and hides you from public marketplace search, but it does NOT unlock tools without payment: pre-assessment link, patient panel, AI, PDFs, exercise programs and clinical chart require an active PRO subscription. The only free exception is an academic partner: an account registered as partner and with the academic toggle enabled by admin. support.pro.faq.rf17.q: A patient remembered extra information after the assessment. How do I add it?

support.pro.faq.rf18.q: How does load control (sRPE) and the planned vs perceived dose comparison work?
support.pro.faq.rf18.a: In the patient record, under "Periodization and load", perceived effort (sRPE) is always answered by the patient: session duration × RPE 0-10 gives the session load, feeding acute (7 days), chronic (28-day average) and ACWR. The coach link plays a different role: it plans the expected dose (target duration × target effort) per track — physio, gym and other sport. The system compares both: if the plan was 40 min × 8 = 320 and the patient perceived 40 min × 7 = 280, the ratio is 0.88 and the work shows as underdosed; 0.90-1.10 is on target; above 1.10, overdosed. You see this in the "Planned vs perceived dose" card (per track, weekly total and session by session), with a badge on the microcycle grid, plus a push alert when the deviation repeats. All calculations are local and deterministic — no AI credits — and the decision to adjust load is always yours.
support.pro.faq.rf19.q: What's the difference between the HEP dose and the coach link? How do they relate?
support.pro.faq.rf21.q: How do I read weekly totals and dose when sessions are still pending?
support.pro.faq.rf21.a: The planned total includes the whole week; the actual total sums sRPE recorded up to today, including extra workouts. The classification and chart compare only completed, answered sessions. On target (1/2 weekly sessions) means one answered session out of two planned for that track, not that the whole week is complete. Underdosed (1/2 weekly sessions) helps review upcoming sessions in the same track according to tolerance and readiness, without automatic compensation. Future or unanswered sessions do not count as underdosed; patients can answer up to 7 days later. This comparison does not send phone notifications.
support.pro.faq.rf19.a: Both feed the same microcycle, through different paths. The HEP derives the dose bottom-up: each exercise adds up per region (sets × reps or isometric hold × load), with strength counting fully, stabilization/proprioception at half and mobility/flexibility outside the count — saving or editing the program recalculates and updates the microcycle's upcoming sessions with duration, target effort and track (physio, gym or other sport). The coach link plans top-down: session by session, with track, duration and target effort, without access to the clinical chart. The patient reports real effort via check-in; the system crosses both on the dose ruler (0.90-1.10 = on target) and feeds acute/chronic load and ACWR. In short: the HEP derives the dose from the exercises; the coach prescribes the session's total dose — both converge in the same calendar. The coach can also import an external workout (text or screenshot): AI lists the exercises, the coach reviews them, picks the weekdays and the dose is calculated with the same HEP rule. Running, cycling, treadmill or games go in the "Cardio" front; morning resting HR (optional in the check-in) is compared with the patient baseline: +5 bpm caution, +7 bpm likely poor recovery. Only sessions already done and answered are compared: a past session without a rating shows as "no answer" and a future one as "upcoming" — neither counts as underdosed. The patient can report a session up to 7 days later through the same check-in link (list of unanswered sessions or extra workout). Planned vs perceived dose does not send phone notifications; it stays in the chart. Shortcut: in the microcycle, tapping a planned session from today or the last 7 days opens the monitored-session entry pre-filled with date, track and target dose. On the chart's front page, text lists show only the last 3 days, grouped by day (tap a day to open its sessions), and charts show the last 7 rolling days; with no recent records, the most recent days with data appear. The full history is under "View history": it opens on the last 45 days, filters by track and period, and lets you go back to earlier periods — nothing is deleted.
support.pro.faq.rf23.q: How do I record cardiorespiratory functional tests (STS, 6MWT, step)?
support.pro.faq.rf23.a: In the patient record, open the collapsed card "Cardiorespiratory assessment (functional tests)", below "Monitored session". Pick 1-min sit-to-stand, 6-min walk or 6-min step and fill rest, peak and recovery, with Borg for breathlessness and leg fatigue. The report shows % predicted (6MWT by the Brazilian equation; STS and step by the table value you enter), SpO₂ and HR recovery alerts and the suggested limiting pattern, always as a suggestion. If you already logged the test as a monitored session (screenshot or typing), pick that session in the form and max HR, minimum SpO₂ and 1-min HR are filled in automatically. Tests do not add to weekly load. The "Sheet" buttons copy a link with instructions and stop criteria. Tests in the period appear in the technical and patient cardiovascular reports.
support.pro.faq.rf22.q: What cardiovascular analysis does the app provide and how do I generate the report?
support.pro.faq.rf22.a: In the patient record, open "Cardiovascular analysis and report" and pick 4, 8 or 12 weeks. You see weekly aerobic minutes against the WHO goal (150 moderate minutes; 1 vigorous minute counts as 2), time in each heart-rate zone, sessions above the profile ceiling, 1-minute heart-rate recovery (a drop of 12 bpm or less is a warning sign, Cole 1999), agreement between perceived effort and heart response, efficiency (metres per beat or watts per bpm) and morning heart rate. For athletic and healthy/active profiles it shows the intensity distribution against the 80/20 model; for hypertensive, cardiac and sedentary profiles, the % of sessions within the prescribed zone (SBC 2020, ACSM). To enrich it, enter the heart rate 1 min after effort, distance or power in the monitored session; in the ceiling card, tick "Uses beta-blocker" to guide by RPE. The buttons create the technical PDF report (session table, caveats and references) and a plain-language patient version you can send from your phone. Interpretation uses fixed rules, with no AI credits, and is always a suggestion, not a diagnosis. The analysis opens in a separate dialog without expanding charts in the patient record. Reports balance achievements and areas to follow up, acknowledging recorded sessions and minutes even below the WHO reference. The patient version starts by recognizing effort and suggests gradual next steps with the physiotherapist, without hiding warnings or assuming inactivity in weeks without records. Open the i icon in the analysis header for profiles, maximum heart rate, ceiling versus target zone, RPE and Borg scales, goals and adaptations (VO₂max and mitochondria). Initial app references: athlete 90%, healthy/active 85%, sedentary 75%, controlled hypertension 70%, cardiac restriction 65% and pulmonary/COPD 70% of estimated maximum heart rate. These are not universal safety limits or targets to reach; manual ceilings are preserved. With test-documented ischemia, consider at least 10 bpm below the ischemic threshold, following the medical report. For pulmonary patients, dyspnea and an individualized SpO₂ target are essential: heart rate and global RPE alone cannot confirm respiratory prescription adherence. Reports include these caveats and profile guidance; they do not measure VO₂max or mitochondria. For athletes and healthy/active patients, PDFs prioritize effort response, recovery and review points. HR/zone coverage and descriptive comparisons lead; WHO remains secondary general-health context. Recovery requires comparable protocols; pace/HR and power/HR do not prove fitness gains, and 80/20 is not mandatory. Alerts and functional tests are retained. The analysis window follows the same logic: cards and charts appear in the profile's priority order — athletic and healthy/active see load (TRIMP), intensity distribution and efficiency first; sedentary patients see the WHO reference and light base first; hypertensive, cardiac and pulmonary patients see the prescribed zone and recovery first. Only the presentation order changes; the calculations are the same. The heart-rate ceiling reads the registered birthdate and conditions and medication from the latest health record (assessment or General health). Caveats appear even without a birthdate. Without age, no bpm ceiling is invented; the manual ceiling and clinician-selected profile are preserved. Recorded hypertension does not establish that it is controlled.
support.pro.faq.rf20.q: Can I enter the patient's heart rate monitor data myself?
support.pro.faq.rf20.a: Yes. In the patient record, under Load and readiness, use "Log monitored session". Upload a screenshot from the monitor app (chest strap, watch or pulse oximeter) for AI reading, or type duration, RPE, average and max HR, minutes per zone and SpO₂. Two loads are shown: sRPE (duration × RPE) and TRIMP (minutes in each HR zone × weight 1 to 5). If the patient also checks in for the same date and track, both become a single session, never counted twice in ACWR: your RPE is used and theirs is kept as the patient's perception.
support.pro.faq.rf25.q: How do I apply the SRS-22r (scoliosis / thoracic spine)?
support.pro.faq.rf25.a: The SRS-22r is a validated complementary questionnaire on the impact of the spinal condition on daily life (22 items, 1–5, higher = better). AI suggests it when the anamnesis mentions scoliosis, kyphosis, thoracic spine, brace or fusion, and you can apply it manually or send it by link. Results show an overall mean and the Function, Pain, Self-image, Mental health and Satisfaction domains; domains below 3 are highlighted. There is no universal cut-off: use it as a baseline and reassess to track change.
support.pro.faq.rf27.q: How do I book a multi-hour appointment (e.g. a course from 8am to 5pm)?
support.pro.faq.rf27.a: Set Start and End when booking — the duration is calculated automatically, with shortcuts (30 min, 50 min, 1h, 2h, All day). On the calendar the card spans the whole period and overlapping items sit side by side. When importing a screenshot, the end time is read when visible and can be edited on each row before importing. On mobile, touch and hold a card for half a second to drag it; a quick tap opens it and swiping just scrolls.
support.pro.faq.rf26.q: How do I export standalone dynamometry or questionnaire reports?
support.pro.faq.rf26.a: In the patient record, use Generate PDF report in Dynamometry or Questionnaires. Select the assessment date and questionnaire. Complementary instruments, including SRS-22r, have a button beside each result. PDFs use saved data only, with patient, date, branding and responsible professional; no AI credits are used. Save dynamometry changes before exporting.
support.pro.faq.rf28.q: How do I import mobility and flexibility measurements?
support.pro.faq.rf28.a: In the Joint mobility and flexibility section, tap Import from image/PDF and send up to 6 photos, screenshots or PDFs of goniometry, inclinometry or flexibility tests. AI fills rows in degrees or cm without erasing typed data; review and save. Reading uses AI credits.
support.pro.faq.rf29.q: Are my notes used in the clinical impression and hypothesis?
support.pro.faq.rf29.a: Yes. Your additional clinical observations, written test/exam findings (including negative findings) and complementary questionnaires such as SRS-22r guide the clinical impression and hypothesis and appear in the report. Session notes are not used in the clinical impression. To update an older assessment, use Regenerate (uses AI credits).
support.pro.tool.spine_maigne.title: Maigne star in the record and PDF
support.pro.tool.spine_maigne.desc: When recorded during manual assessment, the star appears beside ROM with date, region, level and notes; previous exams remain available. The assessment PDF includes that exam, and the evolution report includes exams within the selected period. The biomechanical hypothesis is revisable and does not replace safety screening or neurological examination.
support.pro.faq.rf30.q: Can I assess patients without pain for prevention or follow-up?
support.pro.faq.rf30.a: Yes. Select “I have no pain — I seek prevention or follow-up” at the start of the link or manual anamnesis. Posture remains a goal. The optional map records historical injury or attention sites, not painful areas. Pain intensity, mechanism and automatic pain questionnaires are hidden. Safety and health screening remain; professional-selected questionnaires such as SRS-22r can still be applied. Purpose and goals appear in the record and report without an unmeasured pain score. For attention sites marked on the link, only the daily-activity items of that region's questionnaires are applied (e.g. shoulder SPADI without pain items); pain-framed questionnaires such as ODI and NDI are not used. For the spine (cervical, thoracic, lumbar) the PSFS is applied: the patient writes up to 3 activities and rates ability 0–10.
support.pro.faq.recurring_appointments.a: Yes. When creating an appointment, use "Does not repeat" to pick weekly, chosen weekdays, every 2 weeks or monthly, and when it ends (after N sessions or on a date; up to 60 sessions or 6 months). Dates already booked at that time are skipped and reported. In screenshot import, "Repeat selected" applies to all checked items. When deleting, choose only this one or this and following; completed sessions are kept.

When enabled, the signature image belongs to the issuer and is saved in My account. A missing council never replaces a staff issuer with the owner.
support.pro.tool.report_identity.title: Full name and council on reports
support.pro.tool.report_identity.desc: Clinic staff enter their full name in My account → Clinic report identity. If applicable, select CREFITO, CREF, CRM or Other and enter the number and region; otherwise select No council. Owners and administrators can also edit these details with the pencil in Team. Each staff member saves their own signature in My account → Digital signature, by upload or drawing on screen. Details are scoped to each clinic and do not require a personal PRO subscription. Solo PRO reports use the name and CREFITO from the professional's own profile.
support.pro.tool.acl_preoperative.title: ACL preoperative preparation (restricted beta)
support.pro.tool.acl_preoperative.desc: Administrator-only during validation. Explicitly record ACL preoperative preparation in follow-up goal details, history, complaint or planned surgeries; knee location alone is insufficient. Activate the journey and review the optional planned date and restrictions. Three preparation stages have progressive goals, never surgical clearance. Future postoperative stages are viewable in the same journey, but become current only after recording the performed surgery date, graft and restrictions. Planned dates count days until surgery, never postoperative days. Painless assessments offer complementary questionnaires only by individual professional choice, not blanket recommendations; removing KOOS items does not automatically preserve validation. The journey can be inserted into free-text/referral reports.

support.pro.faq.rf_trial.q: How does the 7-day PRO free trial work?
support.pro.faq.rf_trial.a: The PRO page has two buttons: "Start 7-day free trial" and "Subscribe to PRO now". With the trial, you add your card on the secure Stripe checkout, pay R$ 0.00 today and use PRO for 7 days. Before it ends, Stripe emails you a reminder. If you don't cancel, the first charge for your chosen plan (monthly or annual) happens on day 8. To cancel at no cost, use the email link or "Manage subscription" in your Aliv.iA profile, in one click. The trial is once per account; previous PRO subscribers are charged normally. "Subscribe to PRO now" charges immediately. During the trial, AI has 5 credits; once the subscription starts, all plan credits unlock. To unlock earlier, use "Activate PRO subscription now" (charged immediately).
